tracks.narration: A diode that fights back when you push too hard — meet the Zener.
A Zener has an ordinary forward knee — but in reverse, it breaks down sharply at minus V Z and conducts hard.
Wire a Zener across the output with a series resistor — once the input pushes above V Z, the Zener clamps the output and the resistor soaks up the rest.
Feed in a sine wave taller than V Z. The output rides the sine where it stays below the clamp, but the peaks get sheared off flat at V Z.
The Zener acts like a voltage ceiling — anything above V Z gets clipped, anything below passes through unchanged.
